Contradiction! Going right would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order), and that's the only legal move. So my guess (left from number 4) was wrong, so the line must go up.

I can't rule out up or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going down, the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4); going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,1); going down, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,3). So the line goes up.
Going up leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Going up leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
Going right would leave both number 10 and cell (4,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
The line must go left: right is number 12, which comes later.
Going right would cut off the bottom-left corner (4 cells). So the line goes down.
Cell (6,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
